name: bus_connectors
title: Bus connectors
purpose: Spacecraft bus: 5 V power on a JST XH 2-pin (3 A) and RS-485 on a JST GH 6-pin

sources.title: JST XH connector catalogue page (eXH.pdf)
sources.read: ratings and the B2B-XH-A part table

sources.title: JST GH connector catalogue page (eGH.pdf)
sources.read: ratings and the SM06B-GHS-TB part table

sources.title: Pixhawk Connector Standard DS-009
sources.read: p4 connector series, p5 serial port pinout

parts.quote: "Current rating: 3 A AC/DC（AWG #22）", "2.5 mm pitch"; part table "2 B2B-XH-A". Pin 1 5 V, pin 2 GND (our assignment)

jstgh: "Current rating: 1.0 A AC/DC（AWG #26）", part "SM06B-GHS-TB"; ds009: "It uses the JST GH series which offers a latch lock mechanism at small size", serial pinout 1 VCC +5V, 2 TX, 3 RX, 4 CTS, 5 RTS, 6 GND. Ours (no RS-485 pinout in DS-009): 1 unused, 2 A, 3 B, 4-5 unused, 6 GND

layout.rules: Both at the bottom edge: the GH's opening (the +y side of KiCad's footprint) faces out; the XH is vertical (wire from above).

open_questions: The GH's 1.0 A per pin is why power has its own XH connector.
The GH pin assignment is ours: DS-009 defines no RS-485 port. A and B sit on DS-009's TX/RX positions, pin 1 (+5 V there) is left unconnected so a Pixhawk cable can't feed 5 V into the bus lines.
